title: One basis lemma per topology: box and product (Munkres Theorem 19.2)
intent: State Munkres Theorem 19.2 — the box basis and the product basis are each a basis for their topology — as a two-conjunct statement, and give each conjunct its own named lemma (Theorem_19_2_box, Theorem_19_2_product) proved earlier in the same theory, so the parent proof is nothing but one rule application per case to the shared hypothesis hB.

parent.name: Theorem_19_2
parent.statement:
theorem Theorem_19_2:
  assumes hB: "\<forall>i\<in>I. basis_for (X i) (B i) (T i)"
  shows "basis_for (top1_PiE I X)
           {top1_PiE I U | U. \<forall>i\<in>I. U i \<in> B i}
           (top1_box_topology_on I X T)"
    and "basis_for (top1_PiE I X)
           {top1_PiE I U | U. (\<forall>i\<in>I. U i = X i \<or> U i \<in> B i) \<and> finite {i \<in> I. U i \<noteq> X i}}
           (top1_product_topology_on I X T)"

children.name: Theorem_19_2_box
children.statement:
theorem Theorem_19_2_box:
  assumes hB: "\<forall>i\<in>I. basis_for (X i) (B i) (T i)"
  shows "basis_for (top1_PiE I X)

           (top1_box_topology_on I X T)"
children.closed_by: by (rule Lemma_13_2) — the child assembles Lemma_13_2's four assumptions (hTopBox, hCcT, hTX, hrefine) and ends with `show ?thesis by (rule hBF[unfolded Cc_def])`
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: the box-topology case: the box basis {top1_PiE I U | U. every U i in B i} is a basis for the box topology, given each B i is a basis for T i

  shows "basis_for (top1_PiE I X)
           {top1_PiE I U | U. (\<forall>i\<in>I. U i = X i \<or> U i \<in> B i) \<and> finite {i \<in> I. U i \<noteq> X i}}
           (top1_product_topology_on I X T)"
children.closed_by: by (rule Lemma_13_2) — the child assembles the same four assumptions (hTopProd, hCcT, hTX, hrefine) and ends with `show ?thesis by (rule hBF[unfolded Cc_def])`
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: the product-topology case: the finite-support product basis is a basis for the product topology, given each B i is a basis for T i

applicability.goal_shape: A theorem stated as a conjunction of per-construction cases — here `basis_for (top1_PiE I X) … (top1_box_topology_on I X T)` and `basis_for (top1_PiE I X) … (top1_product_topology_on I X T)` — over one shared hypothesis context (`\<forall>i\<in>I. basis_for (X i) (B i) (T i)`). Each case is a near-copy of the same proof shape, differing only in the topology constructor.
applicability.use_when: there is a family of constructions (box/product, per compiler pass, per crunch component) each needing the same statement, and each construction's proof is long enough to deserve its own lemma; the parent is then a trivial wrapper that applies the matching lemma to each conjunct.
applicability.avoid_when: the cases share a genuinely common sub-proof that should be factored into a third shared lemma first (as Lemma_13_2 is here, shared by both children); or the cases are so short that a single `intro conjI` with two in-place proofs is clearer than two named lemmas.

consequences: Each per-construction lemma restates the shared hypothesis exactly (both children carry the same `assumes hB: \<forall>i\<in>I. basis_for (X i) (B i) (T i)`), so the parent's `[OF hB]` instantiates each uniformly; a child that adds, drops or reorders a hypothesis breaks the parent's one-line application. The parent adds no content beyond the two rule applications, so if a child's statement drifts from the parent's conjunct the parent silently fails. The two children are independent (neither cites its sibling) but both close through Lemma_13_2, so a defect there breaks both at once. The file maintains this one-box-plus-one-product convention for every theorem of section 19 (19.3, 19.4, 19.5), so the pairing itself is the reusable structure, not any single theorem.
